name: Serug
overview: Serug is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the son of Reu. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him beyond his lineage. His role is noted within the genealogy outlined in Genesis 11.
namesAndTitles: The name Serug means 'descendant' or 'younger branch,' reflecting a generational position rather than a divine title. This proper name, as recorded in Genesis 11:20, was not given by God but is significant in tracing biblical ancestry.
familyAndRelationships: Serug is explicitly recorded as the son of Reu and the father of Nahor, establishing his place within the ancestral line leading to later prominent biblical figures. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Serug's importance lies in his position within the genealogical record in Genesis, linking the generations between Reu and Nahor. This lineage is critical for understanding the ancestry of the patriarchs and God's unfolding plan through the descendants of Shem. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the covenant line through successive generations.
